answer_raw:
Rent where you are now to maintain mobility and liquidity for your move.

Buying property in a two-year window is risky because housing markets vary dramatically by location, and 2026 presents no clear-cut winner for buyers facing high prices and elevated borrowing costs [3][5]. A decision that makes sense in one city may not apply in another, and you face the uncertainty of whether your local market will be stable when you are ready to leave [5].

Since you are planning a relocation, staying liquid is vital. Most expats starting fresh in Latin America take only 2–4 checked bags and ship nothing because furniture is cheap locally and shipping is expensive [4]. Renting keeps you from being tied to a fixed asset and heavy furniture when you decide to move.

Your decision should also account for the financial shift you'll experience once you arrive. In Latin America, local labor, food, and real estate are priced for local economies, meaning your US income will buy far more there [6]. Keeping your capital accessible will allow you to navigate the transition—such as meeting residency thresholds like Ecuador's Rentista Visa, which requires $1,446/month as of March 2026 [6]—without the friction of selling a home in a shifting US market.
